title: Brackets With Wildcards
statement:
`text` contains only the characters `(`, `)` and `*`. Each `*` is a **wildcard** that you may turn into `(`, into `)` or into **nothing** (remove it). The text is **valid** if after replacing every `*` the brackets are balanced: every `(` has a matching `)` after it, every `)` has a matching `(` before it, and they nest properly. An empty text is valid.

Return `true` if some choice for the wildcards makes the text valid.

examples.explanation: Turn the `*` into `)`: the text becomes `(())`, which is balanced.
A `)` at the very start can never be matched.

hints.nudge: Trying all 3^k replacements is far too slow. Instead of one count of 'open brackets', keep a RANGE: the smallest and the largest number of open brackets that the text so far could have.
hints.pattern: Track low and high: `(` raises both, `)` lowers both, `*` lowers low (as `)`) and raises high (as `(`). If high ever becomes negative the text is invalid; keep low at least 0. At the end the text is valid if low is 0.
hints.pseudocode:
low = 0; high = 0
for c in text:
  if c == '(': low += 1; high += 1
  elif c == ')': low -= 1; high -= 1
  else: low -= 1; high += 1
  if high < 0: return false
  low = max(low, 0)
return low == 0
hints.walkthrough: Every choice of wildcards gives one possible number of open brackets after each prefix, and all the possible values form a range of whole numbers (changing one star by one step changes the count by 1 or 2 in a connected way, and you can always avoid going below 0 by turning a star into nothing). So you only need the smallest and the largest possible count. `(` adds one to both; `)` subtracts one from both; a `*` can be `)` (subtract), nothing (same) or `(` (add), so low goes down by one and high goes up by one. If high drops below 0, even the best choice has too many `)`: invalid. A count below 0 is not possible, so clamp low at 0 (you would have used the star as nothing instead). At the end, a count of exactly 0 must be reachable: low == 0.
